Our Service Process

How we ensure quality and reliability in every job.

1. Initial Inspection & Diagnosis

Upon receiving a service call, our team arrives on-site to perform a visual and mechanical inspection. We check logs, error codes, and run diagnostic tests to pinpoint the issue quickly.

2. Root Cause Analysis

We don’t just swap parts. We identify *why* the part failed. Was it corrosion? Scaling? Low oil pressure? Our methodology involves finding the root cause to prevent recurrence.

3. Technical Proposal & Quotation

We provide a transparent, itemized quotation for the repair. Whether it’s a compressor overhaul or gas charging, you will know exactly what you are paying for.

4. Expert Repair & Spares Replacement

Using genuine spare parts from brands like Danfoss, Bitzer, and Emerson, our certified technicians execute the repair. We adhere to strict safety standards during all operations.

5. Testing & Commissioning

After repair, we don’t just leave. We load-test the chiller, monitor parameters like superheat and subcooling, and ensure the system is running at peak efficiency before handing it back to you.

Troubleshooting Common Errors

Understanding these codes helps in effective communication with our technicians.

Fault Condition Technical Cause Recommended Solution
HP Trip (High Head Pressure) Scaled condenser tubes, non-condensables in system, or cooling tower fan failure. Perform mechanical tube cleaning (descaling), purge air from the system, and repair cooling tower fans.
LP Trip (Low Suction Pressure) Refrigerant leak, starved evaporator, or Electronic Expansion Valve (EXV) failure. Conduct nitrogen leak test to find leaks, check superheat settings, and replace or calibrate the EXV.
Compressor Flood Back Low load condition, TXV stuck open, allowing liquid to hit the compressor. Adjust superheat settings, check load balance, and ensure the expansion valve is modulating correctly.
Oil Failure Trip Foaming oil, failed oil pump, clogged strainer, or low oil level. Check crankcase heater, replace the oil filter, and top up with the correct grade of refrigeration oil.
Surge (Centrifugal) High lift condition, low flow, or condenser fouling. Analyze the surge map, check condenser approach, and verify VFD operation.
